decision: Which approach best resolves: WF-098's research says the expiry check is a background job: 'If a buyer hasn't accepted or signed a quote by the expiration date, it'll expire.' It also says reminder dispatch is a scheduled job evaluating sent and published quotes relative to the send timestamp and the expiration date. This product has no background worker, has no thread it can start at import time, and requires every write's audit row to name a route the app actually serves. What drives the expiry check and the reminder dispatch?

candidate_solutions.explicit_sweep_route_over_a_movable_cloc: Two explicit POST routes, one for the expiry check and one for the reminder dispatch, both named in their own audit rows. The rules are pure functions of the stored send timestamp, the expiration date, the account timezone and the reminder ledger, and the routes evaluate them. A test moves the clock by hand, so every boundary is reachable. A quote nobody sweeps is still readable past its deadline and the page shows it as due, which is a visible gap rather than a silent one.
candidate_solutions.evaluate_on_every_read: Derive the expired state and the due reminders from the clock on every read of the quote list and the quote detail. No job at all. But a read that changes nothing reports a state the store does not hold, and nothing can write the 'Quote expired' activity or move the quote to Expired, because a GET must not mutate.
candidate_solutions.background_thread_started_at_import_time: A daemon thread on a timer inside the domain module. Matches the research's word 'background job' most literally. But the thread needs a clock no test can move, it opens no request to attribute its writes to, and its audit rows would name no route, which is the exact defect the feature contract names by name.

  frontend/src/features/wf-098-expire-a-quote-and-auto-send-buyer-reminders/primitives.jsx
  orchestration/decisions/wf098-jev-audit.jsonl

Four additive modules inside the existing quoting-proposals package. Its five pre-existing
files (__init__.py, vocabulary.py, rules.py, inferences.py, engine.py, shipped by WF-093
in commit 25e5fda) are not edited. A test asserts the two sets do not overlap.

WHAT IT DOES
23 routes under /api/wf-098. The researched flow, in order:
  Step 1  PUT /rooms/{room_id}/settings sets a default expiration period bounded at 1 to
          365 days. The bound is the research's own and is checked before any row is
          written, so a rejected setting leaves nothing behind.
  Step 2  The reminder schedule is one row per rule, created, patched and deleted by id.
          Each rule names one of the research's two offsets, "Days after sending quote"
          or "Days before expiration date", and the two are never converted into one
          another. GET .../preview is the researched Preview reminder email surface.
  Step 3  POST /rooms/{room_id}/quotes tracks a quote with the research's three separate
          header controls: a date picker value, a label, and the Expiration date switch.
          A stated date wins over the account default; the switch off beats both.
  Step 4  A past effective date is accepted, never refused, and the projection reports
          sign_by_deadline so a reader knows why the deadline reads the way it does.
  Step 5  POST /rooms/{room_id}/reminders evaluates every rule against every quote and
          records a row per decision. POST /rooms/{room_id}/expiry-check moves every quote
          whose deadline passed and whose buyer did not act to expired.

RESEARCHED RULES ENFORCED, each with its own test named after the sentence
  "between 1 and 365 days"        the default window, inclusive at both ends
  "Any new quotes created after the setting is turned on will automatically use the
   configured expiration date"    the default reaches new quotes only; the instant the
                                   default was set is stored to scope it
  "a past Effective date is allowed"  accepted, and the expiration date reads as a sign-by
                                   deadline
  "If a quote is accepted or signed before the expiration date, but hasn't been
   countersigned or paid, the quote won't expire"  the survival predicate is exactly
                                   accepted, e_signed, marked_signed, each at or before the
                                   deadline. Countersigned and paid are accepted as stored
                                   values and do not save the quote. Two tests assert both
                                   halves.
  "the buyer loses the ability to accept"  the acceptance route refuses on an expired
                                   quote, reading the derived state so it does not depend
                                   on the check having run
  "expired quotes can still be downloaded, cloned, voided or archived"  nothing is deleted;
                                   quotes_deleted is reported as 0 and void and archive
                                   still work on an expired quote
  "Void: the quote link URL will be deactivated"  one field, link_active
  "Archive: unpublished, hidden from the index, prevents buyers from accessing"  three
                                   separate fields
  "resending counts as a new send (consuming e-signature quota again)"  a send count and a
                                   separate quota count, both incremented, both reported
  "Reminder schedule ... Days after sending quote or Days before expiration date"  two
                                   stored kinds, the vendor's own label served beside each
  "Reminder send time, in the account time zone"  stored as a wall clock HH:MM and never
                                   as an instant; the due instant takes the local date and
                                   places that reading on it. A test shows 09:00 in +05:30
                                   is 03:30 UTC and that two zones fire the same rule at
                                   two different instants.
  "Send automated reminders to quote recipients"  a stored toggle, defaulting on
  "logged as Quote expired"  the activity is written with that exact name
  "reminder + expiration events are exposed as quote activities"  activities are rows
  "no documented public write API on the pages read"  the settings route is the store and
                                   the gap is served in the vocabulary, on every dispatch
                                   response and on the page

THREE THINGS THE RESEARCH NAMED AS SEPARATE, KEPT SEPARATE
  Expiry, void and archive are three outcomes with three sentences. A voided quote reports
  link_active false and buyer_access true; an archived one reports all three. Over HTTP:
  one quote voided then archived reports state voided and carries both flag sets.
  Sending is a count, not a boolean.
  Each reminder rule fires once per quote, keyed on the rule id, so two rules with the
  same day count are still two reminders and a deleted rule's ledger rows survive it.

declared_unverified: No browser was attached to this session, so the page was not looked at in one. The frontend evidence is the build, the test run, the lint pass and the design-floor script, all of which read source rather than a rendered page.
Contrast ratios, the 375/768/1024/1440 breakpoints and keyboard reachability are not measured. tools/check_design_floor.py says so itself: those need computed styles from a render.

The IANA timezone branch was not exercised against a real zone database. The tests cover the fixed-offset branch and the documented fallback to UTC; zoneinfo may be absent on this host, which is the case the fallback exists for.

The named time zone Asia/Kolkata is in the tests as a string and the response reports it as resolved or not depending on what this host has installed. That is the behaviour under test, not a claim about every host.

No vendor integration was called. The research names HubSpot transactional email and the PandaDoc auto-reminder endpoints; this product sends no HTTP, so every response says sent_by_this_product false and the gap is stated on the page.
The expiring-soon window of 7 days is this build's figure. The research names the filter and not the window, and the vocabulary says so.
Coverage was measured while four other agents ran on the same machine, so the whole-suite wall time is contention-inflated. The percentages are per-file and are not affected.
state.requirements: A feature adds files and edits no shared file. All reads and writes go through dsr.deps / RecordStore / AuditedDatabase so every mutation writes its audit row in the same transaction. Payloads stay schema-flexible JSON: no migration, no typed column, the envelope untouched. The feature owns a unique route prefix with no colliding concrete (method, path) pair. Tests exist and the whole suite is green. The frontend page builds, is discovered by the glob, and meets the design floor.

verdict.instructions: Should this change land on main? Weigh the balance of the questions above rather than deciding on your own: where contract_compliance, audit_integrity and design_floor are all healthy and the evidence questions show broad coverage, answer merge with the confidence that warrants. Items listed as unverified are declared context to weigh, not defects in themselves -- but a change whose coverage is genuinely thin, or which was recovered from a base far behind main and not reconciled, is fix.
